Risk officer read: this is a pass, or at most a minimal probe.

Why: the curve shows bundle_share 0.52, meaning roughly half the curve was bundled buys, which is a warning sign despite the ORGANIC label. Its last-15-minute return of +67% was a sharp run-up. Drawdown is only 21% from the 30-min high, so a 20% stop would sit right on normal noise. Pool depth of 156 SOL keeps a $20 round trip near the 1.4-5% cost range, but exit slippage on a 2,389-buyer, 1,618-seller churn is hard to forecast. Sell-to-buy ratio of 0.92 right after graduation means sellers were nearly matching buyers.

Refuse any size if the bundle share is confirmed as operator-linked, or if the pool drops much below 150 SOL. If the desk insists on trading, use $5, a 25% stop, and a 30-minute hold.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for WISP is its breadth of participation. In the last 15 minutes, 2,389 buyers and 1,618 sellers traded, with $190k in volume and a 67% return, which suggests wide, not concentrated, interest. Top-3 curve concentration is only 6.6%, the top-5 buyer share after graduation is 15.7%, and the post-graduation buy flow of 115 SOL came from 330 buyers, so no single wallet is carrying the price. No airdrop dump was seen, and the coin is alive, 2.2x over 30 minutes, and only 21% off its 30-minute high.

The case has real holes, though. Sells are 92% of buys in the first two minutes after graduation, net flow over 15 minutes is thin at 52 SOL against $190k of volume, and the launch bot and 52% bundle share on the curve are warning signs. A $162k market cap with a 156 SOL pool means a $20 ticket moves the price, and the round trip costs 1.4-5.1%. I can make a case for demand persisting, but not a strong one, and the base rates for coins 30 minutes past graduation argue against entering now.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a distribution after the run. WISP is up 2.23x over 30 minutes, but the last 15 minutes show sell_sol of 751 against buy_sol of 804, with net flow only +52 SOL and 1,618 sellers against 2,389 buyers. Momentum is fading into a heavy sell wall. The curve also shows bundle_share of 0.52, meaning about half the early supply came through bundled buys, and the first 2 minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.92 with a launch bot present. That points to coordinated early accumulation now being unwound. The 21% drawdown from the high has already started. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a 156 SOL pool, a small pullback would be eaten by fees and impact. Skip.
